children: The recent selloff in the artificial-intelligence trade is a realignment of expectations and valuations, rather than an indication that the investment cycle is fundamentally broken, Julius Baer analyst Enrico Chinello writes in a note. Financing worries and fears of tighter AI regulations, questions around the long-term role of Nvidia in providing financial support to the ecosystem after Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia's CEO, and a potentially more hawkish outlook from the Fed contributed to the problem for markets, Chinello says. Anthropic's blockbuster debut wasn't enough to calm these concerns, with questions persisting around its business model and the sustainability of infrastructure expenditure, Chinello says. Still, the outlook for AI spending remains strong with a growing pipeline of data centers, he says. Nvidia's board reinstated Huang as CEO overnight. (kimberley.kao@wsj.com)
